{
"Clean Code": "Source code that is written in a clear, structured, and disciplined manner, making it both readable and maintainable. It emphasizes simplicity, clarity, and adherence to best practices in software design.",
"Readable Code": "Code that can be easily understood by humans due to its clear structure, meaningful naming, and logical organization. Readability enables developers to quickly grasp the intent and functionality of the code.",
"Maintainable Code": "Code that is designed to be easily modified, extended, or debugged over time without introducing errors. It supports long-term software evolution through clarity, modularity, and well-defined abstractions.",
"Function": "A reusable, self-contained block of code that performs a specific task and may return a value. In clean code, functions should be small, focused, and dedicated to a single responsibility.",
"Single Responsibility Principle": "A design principle stating that a class or module should have only one reason to change, meaning it should encapsulate a single, well-defined responsibility. It promotes modularity, cohesion, and ease of maintenance.",
"Class": "A blueprint in object-oriented programming that defines the structure and behavior of objects through attributes and methods. Classes should adhere to the Single Responsibility Principle to remain cohesive and maintainable.",
"Meaningful Name": "An identifier for a variable, function, class, or other code element that clearly conveys its purpose or intent. Meaningful names avoid random characters and abbreviations, aiding code comprehension.",
"Comment": "A human-readable annotation in source code that is ignored by the compiler or interpreter. In clean code, comments should explain the reasoning behind decisions rather than restate what the code does.",
"Method": "A function defined within a class that implements part of the class's behavior and typically operates on its instance data. Methods represent the actions that objects of a class can perform.",
"Variable": "A named storage location in code that holds a value, which may change during program execution. Variables are used to represent and manage state within a program.",
"State": "The current values and conditions held by a program or object at a given moment, typically represented through variables. State determines how the program behaves and responds to inputs.",
"Code Comprehension": "The cognitive process by which developers read, interpret, and understand source code. It is facilitated by meaningful names, clear structure, and appropriate documentation.",
"Class Behavior": "The set of actions and operations that instances of a class can perform, defined by its methods. Class behavior reflects how objects interact with data and other components in the system.",
"Abbreviation": "A shortened form of a word or phrase used in identifiers, which can obscure meaning and reduce code clarity. Clean code discourages abbreviations in favor of full, descriptive, and meaningful names."
}
